breakdown.description: A perfectly incompressible fluid would imply infinite sound speed; a finite sound speed requires finite compressibility (finite bulk modulus).
breakdown.reason: The agent did not treat water as perfectly incompressible (which would give infinite speed). Instead, it used a finite bulk modulus (K = 2.2×10^9 Pa) in the formula c = sqrt(K/ρ), effectively correcting the incompressibility assumption and producing a finite, physically meaningful result matching the ground truth.

breakdown.description: Water is slightly compressible, so c should be computed from bulk modulus and density.
breakdown.reason: The agent correctly computed the speed of sound using c = sqrt(K/ρ) with K = 2.2 GPa and ρ = 998 kg/m³, yielding c ≈ 1485 m/s. This matches the ground truth's approach of treating water as slightly compressible and using bulk modulus and density.
